# Your own background clips

Drop `.mp4` loops in this folder and they appear in **step 3, Background** inside
ShortGeek. Any aspect ratio works: clips are cropped to fill the 1080x1920 frame,
never stretched. Each render starts the clip at a random point, so reusing one
across several videos does not look like the same footage twice.

In an installed copy this folder lives beside your other ShortGeek data, at:

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\ShortGeek\backgrounds\custom
```

The **Backgrounds** page in the app opens it for you, and can copy a clip straight
in, so you never have to find it by hand.

## Where to get clips

ShortGeek deliberately ships with none. Stock sites let you *use* their footage
freely, but they do not let anyone redistribute the files, and bundling a library
of somebody else's clips inside an installer is redistribution.

These are free, no account needed for downloading, and all allow commercial use:

- **Pexels Videos** — https://www.pexels.com/videos/
- **Pixabay Videos** — https://pixabay.com/videos/
- **Videvo** — https://www.videvo.net/ (check the per-clip licence, some need credit)
- **Coverr** — https://coverr.co/

Search for "vertical" or filter to portrait to save yourself the cropping.

## Two things worth knowing

**Read the licence on the clip you download, not the one on the site's front page.**
Several libraries mix licences, and a few require attribution.

**Footage you shot yourself is always the safest option**, and on short-form it
usually performs better than stock, because it looks like a person rather than a
template.
